# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 12 (Bu-Vb Np12)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Np12
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 12
**Title (English, from literature):** Making a blanket entirely of black wool

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Suddhakāla Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 12) is a disciplinary rule within the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule lays down that any monk who makes a blanket or rug entirely out of black sheep's wool commits an offense requiring forfeiture (*nissaggiya*) and formal confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. A modern English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
This training rule is broadly attested across early Buddhist monastic lineages. Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra*, as well as Prātimokṣa and Vinayavibhaṅga recensions preserved in Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese from the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka (Np 22), Mahāsāṅghika and Lokottaravāda (Np 11), and Dharmaguptaka traditions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus analysis identifies 436 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 116 texts, reflecting widespread Vinaya legal phrasing shared predominantly with adjacent wool-related rules such as Nissaggiya Pācittiya 11, 13, 14, and 15, as well as Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26 and various Pācittiya rules [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with Tibetan Vinaya literature, such as the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
